column1: The Phillips Curve Revisited: Evidence from arXiv CPI Data

The thesis titled ConocoPhillips' share price model revisited by Ivan Kitov from the Institute for the Geospheres’ Dynamics  Russian Academy of Sciences  revisits a previously established model linking ConocoPhillips' stock price to the difference between the core and headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) in the United States. Initially discovered three years prior  this relationship was statistically reliable and allowed for the prediction of ConocoPhillips' stock price based on CPI differences. The original model  which covered data from 1982 to 2009  was relatively crude  relying on two major CPIs and splitting the data into two segments to account for a trend change between 1998 and 2002. However  the model's predictive power was confirmed with new data available since 2009.

To enhance the model's accuracy  Kitov developed advanced models incorporating smaller components of the headline CPI  such as motor fuel and housing energy  and several Producer Price Indices (PPIs) like crude oil and coal  which are inherently related to ConocoPhillips and other energy companies. These advanced models demonstrated lower modeling errors and better statistical properties  significantly improving the original approach's predictive power  reliability  and accuracy.

The thesis also revisits the quasi-linear trend in the CPI difference  which allows for accurate predictions of ConocoPhillips' stock prices over a five to ten-year horizon. The study assumes that the future of selected stocks is not entirely unpredictable  despite the common belief that all available information is already priced in by market participants. Kitov argues that deterministic models based on various CPIs can describe many companies' stocks  allowing for market outperformance. The existence of unaccounted information does not contradict common wisdom and scientific knowledge  as there are true links between measured variables that remain unknown.

The paper is structured as follows: Section 1 presents linear trends in the difference between the core and headline CPI observed in the past and predicts their evolution over several years. Section 2 predicts the evolution of ConocoPhillips' stock price as a linear function of the CPI difference  validating the original model with newly available estimates. Section 3 extends the set of defining CPIs and introduces PPIs as drivers of ConocoPhillips' stock price  adding a linear time term and an intercept to the model. These improvements allow for a more accurate description  with the best model having a standard error of $3.96 between July 2003 and March 2012.

The concept and data section reveals sustainable quasi-linear trends in the differences between consumer and producer price indices. The difference between the core CPI and the headline CPI can be approximated by a linear time function  with distinct periods of linear time dependence identified from 1960 to 1980  1980 to 1998  and 2002 to 2008. The second period is characterized by a positive slope  while the third has a larger negative slope. The study predicts a new linear trend emerging between 2009 and 2015  mirroring the previous trend between 2002 and 2008.

Kitov's approach to stock pricing assumes that share prices for energy companies are likely driven by changes in overall energy prices  which can be expressed by the headline CPI or its components. Even if a company does not change its production  an overall increase in product prices should manifest in its profit and share price. Conversely  if other prices rise faster than the energy price index  the company may not gain extra pricing power. The study concludes that the original approach has been significantly improved  with advanced models showing higher predictive power  reliability  and accuracy  making it mandatory to apply the advanced approach to ConocoPhillips' stocks.
